method: Each refresh records the Oracle's decisive forecasts (peaking / accelerating / rising / fading) in data/forecast_ledger.json. 48h later the forecast is compared with the actual velocity history and scored hit/miss; when the 48h window holds fewer than 2 actual snapshots the call is marked unverifiable (data gap — not a miss) with its reason recorded. Nothing is backfilled — the log starts 2026-10-11, so the first resolutions land 48h after that.

resolution_rules.rising_accelerating: hit if the actual velocity slope over the 48h window after the forecast is >= +1.5/hr (the classifier's own rising threshold)
resolution_rules.peaking: hit if the highest velocity in the 48h window stays at/below the forecast-time velocity +2 (the top was called, not blown through)
resolution_rules.fading: hit if the actual velocity slope over the 48h window is <= -1.5/hr (the classifier's own falling threshold)
resolution_rules.unverifiable: the 48h window holds fewer than 2 actual velocity snapshots (data gap: topic dropped, series pruned, fetch outage) — counted separately, never folded into the hit rate

hit_rate_note: The Oracle shows its own hit rate once 10 forecasts have resolved decisively; currently 0 decisive.
